_README: Promoted, tracked copy of the run whose numbers are cited. Regenerate with `python -m crest.analysis.promote_leaderboard --run <run_dir>`. summary.json is NOT a substitute: it lacks the primary endpoint, the provenance and the caveats.

provenance.judge_protocol: full-panel (same-family as covariate); blind; median aggregation

totals.n_task_errors_note: CORRECTED 2026-08-01 from 2. The source manifest counted raw errors.jsonl LINES, and this run's two lines share one record_id (C1_evaluation_benchmarking_04 x gemini_deepresearch_max, written once as agent_error and once as agent_error_after_sweep). One task failed, not two -- the old value made the parts sum to 251 of 250. results.py::finalize_run now de-duplicates, but that fix is forward-only: the on-disk manifest still carries 2, and rejudge.py carries the manifest value forward, so re-judging this run would reintroduce it.

primary_endpoint.definition: min(New, Useful, Surprising), graded on the 1-10 scale

caveats: NO RANKING CLAIM IS MADE. On the science run, per-axis judge severity (3.32/3.20/3.74) EXCEEDED the entire between-entrant spread (2.06), so an ordering is not identifiable from a run of this design. This table is not a leaderboard.

DIFFERENT ITEM SET AND DIFFERENT JUDGE PROMPT from result/leaderboard.json. These are the 50 AI/ML items, and this run is scored under JUDGE_PROMPT_VERSION v3 (hash d4c68e7b) -- the first run under v3, which REMOVED the rule cap that floored Useful at <=3 and softened the 'score ONLY against this list' novelty clause. result/leaderboard.json is v1/null and run 2026-07-31T193800Z was v2, so none of the three are mutually comparable. Paired on 242 byte-identical answers, v2->v3 moved New -0.90, Useful +1.20, and corr(min(N,U,S),Useful) 0.957 -> 0.737.

[CORRECTED 2026-07-31: this caveat had been carried forward verbatim from the v2 run 2026-07-31T193800Z by promote_leaderboard's caveat-preservation step and described THAT run, not this one.] n IS UNEQUAL BUT ONLY BY ONE: claude_shallow / openai_shallow / openai_deepresearch / gemini_shallow n=50, gemini_deepresearch_max n=49. The single missing record is C1_evaluation_benchmarking_04 x gemini_deepresearch_max, a provider failure whose root cause was our own 15-second retry window. It was subsequently generated and scored under the SAME judge prompt v3 and the same panel, and lives in run 2026-08-01T031755Z__crest_aiml__one-item-retry__git0bc15e70__49d901. It is NOT merged here because promote_leaderboard takes a single run directory. Merging it moves only the gemini_deepresearch_max C1 cell materially (3.667 -> 3.800); its primary endpoint moves 5.102 -> 5.100 and no other entrant changes.

[CORRECTED 2026-07-31: this caveat had been carried forward verbatim from the v2 run 2026-07-31T193800Z by promote_leaderboard's caveat-preservation step and described THAT run, not this one.] gemini_shallow BARELY BROWSED. 35 of 50 records returned ZERO web searches and the maximum on any record was 5, for a mean of 1.06 -- against 2.06 for openai_shallow, 4.88 for claude_shallow and 58.45 for gemini_deepresearch_max. The google_search tool IS attached. Treat gemini_shallow on this item set as a largely unretrieved arm. (The carried-forward wording said ZERO on essentially every item, which was true of the v2 run, not this one.)

[CORRECTED 2026-07-31: this caveat had been carried forward verbatim from the v2 run 2026-07-31T193800Z by promote_leaderboard's caveat-preservation step and described THAT run, not this one.] THE ENDPOINT IS NO LONGER LARGELY HARD-RULE COMPLIANCE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF v3. corr(min(N,U,S), Useful) = 0.737 on this run, down from 0.957 under v2 on 242 BYTE-IDENTICAL answers -- the cleanest available demonstration that deleting the Useful cap decoupled the axes, since the answers did not change. Judge rows citing a hard-rule violation average Useful 6.12 against 8.20 for clean rows (n=374 / 373); under v2 the same split was 2.84 vs 8.63. Rule conformance is now scored separately as rule_compliance. NOTE that caveat 2 already stated 0.737 correctly, so this file previously asserted both values for one run.

[CORRECTED 2026-07-31: this caveat had been carried forward verbatim from the v2 run 2026-07-31T193800Z by promote_leaderboard's caveat-preservation step and described THAT run, not this one.] THE RULE GATE IS NO LONGER A judge_openai EFFECT. Firing rate by judge on this run: judge_openai 71.9%, judge_anthropic 71.5%, judge_google 6.8%. The OpenAI/Anthropic gap is 0.4 points, not the 13.5 the carried-forward numbers (77.3 / 63.8 / 4.3) implied. What survives is the judge_google outlier: it cites a violation roughly a tenth as often as the other two, so hard-rule citation remains substantially a judge-identity effect.

[CORRECTED 2026-07-31: this caveat had been carried forward verbatim from the v2 run 2026-07-31T193800Z by promote_leaderboard's caveat-preservation step and described THAT run, not this one.] ZERO truncated records in this run (manifest totals.n_truncated = 0, confirmed by recomputation over all 249). The `truncated` field is present and populated; filtering on it here returns nothing because there is nothing to filter. The 1 truncated claude_shallow record belongs to the v2 run.

Retrieval was LIVE provider web search. Not contamination-controlled; no frozen index exists. The run directory is gitignored, so per-record judge rows and transcripts are not distributed and this file cannot be recomputed from a fresh clone.
